description: Ceiling for the kasirmu-core production line count (Phase 3 P3.4, plan section 11.1). scripts/verify-core-size.py fails when the measured count rises above ceiling. Lowering it is a deliberate edit, exactly as a retired namespace edge leaves scripts/namespace-governance-baseline.json. RAISE HISTORY, kept because the reasoning is the whole point of the file: Raised 2026-10-14 from 37176 to 38703 (+1527) because the growth is legitimate feature work spread across 56 commits, not one misplaced module — see the commit message for the analysis. Extraction was deliberately NOT chosen: audit.rs's four concerns (redaction, rate-limited write, hash chaining, off-device shipping) share a single insert_audit body whose docstring explains why a second writer would leak AUD-06's redacted keys. Raised again 2026-10-19 from 38703 to 39068 (+365), and the analysis is the same shape rather than a new judgement: 15 distinct files contributed net production growth across 952 commits, the largest single contributor is db/assignments.rs at 97 lines (27% of the delta) and the top three sum to 198 (54%), so there is no one misplaced module to extract — the growth is incremental work on assignments, provisioning, products CRUD, profile, sale deduction, CRL and tax assignments. Two caveats a reader should know before crediting this raise: the gate was RED for an unknown period before it was noticed (the doc pass that found it, docs/architecture/module-namespace-firewall.md, had itself been quoting the PREVIOUS ceiling of 37176), and a ceiling that is only ever moved after the fact is a changelog rather than a ratchet — the intended use is to move it deliberately as part of a change that also says why. NOTE: running verify-core-size.py --emit-baseline rewrites this description to a one-line default; if that happens, restore the history from git and re-append, which is exactly what this edit does.
measure: non-blank lines in crates/kasirmu-core/src production .rs files, minus inline #[cfg(test)] mod blocks
